text:
elena: heads up — while QA-ing the saved-search retention test I briefly saw rows from org-id=acme-corp in a different tenant's saved search results :eyes:

sam: wait, really? can you repro or is it transient?

elena: repro 2x. steps: 1) login as org-b tester, 2) open saved search 'payment-failures', 3) see results with org_id: acme-corp in the UI. happened on staging and on a prod-like canary node.

dave: did you grab the network request / response? any headers missing?

elena: pasted request below — headers look like this:

```
GET /api/v1/search/saved?id=pay-failures&limit=25 HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.internal
Accept: application/json
X-Request-ID: req-9f8a
X-Tenant-ID: org-b
Cookie: session=...
```

response included hits where hit.metadata.org_id = "acme-corp"

maya: hmm that header seems present. maybe the cache key at the CDN or the internal cache doesn't include X-Tenant-ID. Fastly config recently got the "edge-opt" tweak in last rollout.

robin: we changed the CDN to cache on path + query only for that rollout to reduce origin load. if saved searches are namespace-scoped by header instead of path/query it would explain cross-tenant leakage.

sam: deploy-bot — any recent deploys touching CDN config or console search handler?

deploy-bot: deployment INF-frontend-2023:edge-opt enabled on 3 hosts at 2023-11-14T17:02:09Z. No server-side search logic changes in that rollout.

dave: ok likely edge cache key omission. mitigation: 1) purge relevant cache keys, 2) immediately disable edge-opt for /api/v1/search/*, 3) add tenant header to cache key.

elena: agree. also add an emergency telemetry check to catch cross-org rows: run a daily job that asserts saved search results contain only expected org_ids for seeded queries.

maya: quick fix pushed to canary: add "X-Tenant-ID" to surrogate-key composition and send purge for /api/v1/search/* on staging and prod-canary. rolling back global edge-opt until we have tests.

robin: we should also audit other endpoints that rely on header scoping (dashboards, runlist, quick-switch). I can parse Fastly logs to find endpoints with cache hits where X-Tenant-ID was absent.

sam: created INF-4287 to track remediation + postmortem, assigned to eng-platform and eng-runtime. cc @security for potential customer notice.

elena: action items: purge + disable edge-opt (maya), add cache-key tests (dave), fastly log audit (robin), telemetry check + postmortem draft (sam). I'll add short notes to the incident doc. :thumbsup:

maya: status update in 30m — patch is on canary, rolling to remaining nodes after smoke checks.

robin: one more thing — add an invariant check in the backend: when serializing saved-search hits, assert all hits have tenant_id == request.tenant_id, and raise a metric if not. saves us from silent leaks in the future.

elena: perfect. thanks all.
